public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic and OpenAI will eventually have to massively cut how many tokens subscribers can use.

statement.excerpt: The problem is that a subsidy is always a losing proposition, which means that at some point Anthropic and OpenAI will have to massively reduce the amount of tokens that people use on their accounts.
statement.document_title: The Subprime AI Crisis Is Here

from_speaker: the amount of tokens that people use on their accounts
our_interpretation: The context concerns included usage on paid subscriptions at both companies.
The ordinary reading is a large reduction in usable subscription allowances, compared with the allowances available when the claim was published. No numerical threshold is supplied.
Comparable measurements must account for model choice, token accounting, billing period and temporary promotions.
The subsidy argument predicts economic pressure requiring the cuts. A temporary service interruption alone would not establish that claim.
criteria.support_condition: Both companies implement large reductions in comparable included subscription usage after publication, with evidence connecting those reductions to the economics of providing the service.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive event establishes that the predicted required cuts cannot occur. An allowance increase or continued generous service for a finite period does not disprove an eventual forecast.
